title: GEM: GPU-Accelerated Emulator-Inspired RTL Simulation
problem: CPU-based RTL simulators face scalability bottlenecks; FPGA emulators are expensive and inaccessible; prior GPU acceleration fails due to heterogeneous circuit partitions conflicting with SIMT parallelism.
motivation: High-speed circuit verification is critical for design closure; democratizing RTL simulation with affordable GPU hardware would accelerate design cycles.
method: GEM creates a virtual Very Long Instruction Word architecture (VLIW — a compact way to represent operations, inspired by FPGA emulator design) that runs on NVIDIA GPUs via CUDA. It maps circuit logic into this VLIW form using a CAD process (computer-aided design) based on FPGA place-and-route — the step that assigns circuit logic to physical locations and routes their connections. This solves two problems that prevented earlier GPU simulators from working: irregular memory access patterns (when threads access memory unpredictably) and thread divergence (when different threads take different execution paths), both of which severely reduce GPU efficiency.
key_novelty: GEM uses a virtual VLIW architecture to let GPUs (which run the same instruction across many threads simultaneously) simulate circuits with heterogeneous parts (different sections needing different processing).
contributions: Novel virtual VLIW architecture enabling efficient GPU-based RTL simulation
Circuit-to-VLIW mapping flow using FPGA CAD-like methodology
Solution to thread divergence and irregular memory access on GPUs
Up to 64x speedup over best CPU simulators
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated RTL simulation via VLIW architecture
